items.followUp: Write one contribution of Al-Jahiz to biology.

rubric.why: Credits Jabir bin Hayan with introducing experimental investigation into scientific research.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that he introduced or used the experimental method in scientific research.

rubric.why: Credits him with writing about plants and animals.
rubric.description: Wrote a book on plants and animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a book or writing about both plants and animals.

modelAnswer: Jabir bin Hayan introduced experimental investigation into scientific research.
He wrote a book on plants and animals.

items.followUp: What is a hypothesis in scientific inquiry?

rubric.why: Identifies observations as information gathered through careful watching.
rubric.description: Information is gathered by carefully observing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing careful watching or observing.

rubric.why: Includes the means used to make observations.
rubric.description: Observations are made using the senses or instruments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning senses or instruments.

modelAnswer: Observations are the information or facts gathered by carefully watching a phenomenon.
They are made using our senses or suitable instruments.

items.followUp: Name two ways in which scientific results can be presented.

rubric.why: Explains that reporting means communicating the findings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the findings are communicated or presented.

rubric.why: Gives a valid format for reporting findings.
rubric.description: Results may be reported using tables, graphs, diagrams, or a written report.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one suitable reporting format.

modelAnswer: Reporting of results is communicating the findings of an investigation to others.
Results may be reported in a research paper or presented using tables, graphs, or diagrams.

rubric.why: Identifies diffusion as movement down a concentration gradient.
rubric.description: Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from higher to lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating movement from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: Distinguishes facilitated diffusion by the involvement of membrane proteins while movement remains down the gradient.
rubric.description: Facilitated diffusion occurs down the concentration gradient with help from membrane proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that membrane proteins assist movement down the concentration gradient.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the net movement of molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Facilitated diffusion is movement down the concentration gradient across a membrane with the help of membrane proteins.

items.followUp: Define exocytosis and name its two main types.

rubric.why: Describes uptake by the plasma membrane forming a vesicle.
rubric.description: Endocytosis is the uptake of material by infolding of the plasma membrane to form a vesicle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing membrane infolding and vesicle formation for uptake.

rubric.description: The two forms are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both forms.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the uptake of material into a cell by infolding of the plasma membrane to form a vesicle.
Its two forms are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.

items.followUp: What are the two main stages of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: Defines the cell cycle as the sequence of events between divisions or through growth and division.
rubric.description: The cell cycle is the series of events from one cell division to the next.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of the cell cycle.

rubric.description: The two major phases are interphase and the division (M) phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both phases.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the series of events that occurs in a cell from one division to the next.
Its two major phases are interphase and the division (M) phase.

items.followUp: What is autolysis, and how can lysosomes bring it about?

rubric.why: Identifies release of lysosomal enzymes as the initiating event.
rubric.description: Lysosomes release their digestive enzymes, often when they rupture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that lysosomal enzymes are released or lysosomes rupture.

rubric.why: Explains that the enzymes digest cell parts and contribute to necrosis.
rubric.description: The enzymes digest cell components, leading to cell destruction or death.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking enzyme digestion of cell material with cell death or necrosis.

modelAnswer: During necrosis, lysosomes may rupture and release their digestive enzymes.
These enzymes digest the cell's components, causing cell destruction and death.

rubric.why: Identifies the absence of a true nucleus in prokaryotes.
rubric.description: Prokaryotes lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that prokaryotes have no true nucleus.

rubric.why: Explains that prokaryotes do not undergo mitosis and may identify their alternative division method.
rubric.description: They reproduce by binary fission rather than mitosis; mitosis requires the eukaryotic division machinery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mitosis is absent and/or that prokaryotes divide by binary fission.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotes lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus and the mitotic machinery found in eukaryotic cells.
Therefore, mitosis does not occur in them; they divide by binary fission.
